source_caption:
More than four decades after its release, Airplane! remains one of the funniest and most influential comedies ever made. Its formula is simple: deliver as many jokes as possible and never give the audience too much time to recover before the next one arrives.

Much of the comedy comes from how seriously the cast treats completely ridiculous situations. Leslie Nielsen is the perfect example. His deadpan performance became one of the defining roles of his career and helped establish a style of comedy he would later become famous for. The film combines this dry delivery with physical comedy, background jokes, visual gags and unapologetically silly humor.

It also became one of the most quotable comedies ever made. Many films followed its approach, including The Naked Gun, Hot Shots! and Loaded Weapon, but Airplane! remains the movie that helped set the standard for the modern comedy. 🎭

source_details.synopsis: Airplane! (alternatively titled Flying High!) is a 1980 American comedy film written and directed by David Zucker, Jim Abrahams, and Jerry Zucker in their directorial debut, and produced by Jon Davison. It stars Robert Hays and Julie Hagerty and features Leslie Nielsen, Robert Stack, Lloyd Bridges, Peter Graves, Lorna Patterson, Stephen Stucker, and Kareem Abdul-Jabbar. It is a parody of the disaster film genre, particularly the 1957 Paramount film Zero Hour!, from which it borrows the plot, central characters, and some dialogue.
